blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Biomimicry

A Velcro, now commonly used instead of buttons and zippers, is probably the most famous example of ‘biomimicry', where technologists turn to nature for inspiration. In 1948, scientist Georges de Mestral was walking through long grass when he noticed that dozens of seeds had attached themselves to his trousers. Under a microscope, de Mestral noted the hook-and-loop system the seed cases used to stick so firmly, and was inspired.

B US biologist Janine Benyus wrote a book on the subject called Biomimicry: Innovation Inspired by Nature. Published in 1997, the book set off the current wave of technology modelled on nature. According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry. 'I think it's an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,' she says, referring to African tribes that found edible plants by observing the dining habits of chimpanzees. But lately we've become more focused on what we can make ourselves. Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: ‘When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn't need other organisms at all,' she says.

C The scientific, industrial, petrochemical and genetic engineering revolutions have repeatedly reinforced the idea that we are liberated from biological constraints. In recent years, however, the illusion that we are independent of nature has been shattered by the spectre of global warming and the looming end to fossil fuel supplies. Since few of us would be willing to forgo the products and services we've grown accustomed to – food, water, shelter, the conveniences that modern technology brings – the challenge is to meet the complex demands of civilisation within the bounds of sustainability. ‘Nature has learnt to fly, live in the depths of the ocean and craft miracle materials,' writes Benyus. ‘Living creatures have done everything we want to do, without guzzling fossil fuel or polluting the planet. What better models could there be?'

D There are no better models, according to Tim Finnigan, a marine engineer at the University of Sydney. In his quest to harness the world's waves and tides for renewable energy more efficiently, Finnigan has taken his cues from aquatic life. With their streamlined bodies and stiff, high tail fins, sharks convert up to 90 per cent of their body energy into forward thrust. Inspired by such efficient hydrodynamics, but turning the theory on its head, Finnigan designed his tidal stream generator: an 18-metre-long biomimetic shark tail with a fin spanning 15 metres. ‘Rather than have a body moving through a stationary fluid, we have fluid that's moving past a stationary body,' says Finnigan.

E Then there's Finnigan's biomimetic forest of giant seaweed. ‘As a diver I've looked at the way motions occur under water in the presence of waves,' he says. 'I see plants that move quite dramatically and yet they never seem to be pulled out, even in the most dramatic waves.' The trouble with conventional designs, according to Finnigan, is that they're made to stand rigidly against the power of the ocean. ‘The structures we try to build in the ocean just never end up being strong enough to survive out there,' says Finnigan. In the manner of aquatic plants and animals, Finnigan's designs respond to changing current or wave conditions by reorienting to maximise energy capture. And in severe weather, to avoid a battering, his wave energy generator will lie flat against the ocean floor.

F While conventional architects were designing buildings dependent on expensive air conditioning systems, when Mick Pearce tried to do the same, he struck a problem. 'We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds. So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.' One day, driving through the grasslands, he saw a large mound created by termites, the ant-like insect common in Africa. He noticed that air entering at the base of the mound was mixed with water drawn from subterranean levels by the termites, causing evaporative cooling. Pearce wanted to reproduce this principle but he needed an alternative system, and in his building massive fans were employed at the base of the structure to lower the temperature of the circulating air. Pearce's termite-inspired cooling system cut energy use to 10 per cent of a similar air-conditioned building.

G Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use energy from the sun to convert water and carbon dioxide into carbohydrates and oxygen. Plants can manage it with humbling ease. But, as the 40 researchers from 11 institutes who have collaborated to form the Australian Artificial Photosynthesis Network have realised, it is very complex. However, there is one aspect working in our favour. In nature, environmental variables like temperature, carbon dioxide and light availability limit the rate of photosynthesis. In a laboratory these variables can be optimized. ‘We don't have to cope with drought or frost. We can work with a highly controlled, specified set of conditions,' says Tom Collings, the group's spokesman.

questionGroups.bodyHtml:
Questions 14–18

Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A–G.

Which paragraph contains the following information?

NB You may use any letter more than once.

ABCDEFG
14 a reference to a natural process that appears simpler than it actually is
15 a description of an invention that can protect itself under extreme conditions
16 the reasons why humans no longer feel they are free from nature
17 a reference to an animal that influenced the diet of some humans
18 specific reasons why science should copy nature

Questions 19–23

Look at the following statements (Questions 19–23) and the list of researchers below.

Match each statement with the correct researcher, A–E.

NB You may use any letter more than once.

19 Designs often fail when they try to resist natural forces.

20 Science has certain key advantages over nature.

21 People have been copying nature for thousands of years.

22 A shortage of money can inspire innovative design.

23 The discovery that humans could produce food themselves caused them to turn away from nature.

List of Researchers
A Georges de Mestral
B Janine Benyus
C Tim Finnigan
D Mick Pearce
E Tom Collings

Questions 24–26

Complete the summary below.

Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.

A building project in Zimbabwe

Mick Pearce designed a cooling system radically different from those usually used by architects. The design of his office block can be compared to that of a termite's 24 . Termites use 25 to cool the air, but in Pearce's system this cooling effect was produced by 26 .

sourceRefs.shuiHtml: 睡着过项目组/2. 所有文章(11.20)[192篇]/103. P2 - Biomimicry 仿生学/103. P2 - Biomimicry 仿生学.html

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 魔术贴，如今被广泛使用来替代纽扣和拉链，可能是“仿生学”最著名的例子，即技术人员向大自然寻求灵感。1948年，科学家乔治·德·梅斯特拉尔在穿过高草丛时，注意到数十颗种子附着在了他的裤子上。在显微镜下，德·梅斯特拉尔注意到种子外壳用来牢牢粘附的钩环系统，并由此受到启发。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 美国生物学家贾尼娜·拜卢斯写了一本关于这一主题的书，名为《仿生学：受自然启发的创新》。该书于1997年出版，引发了当前以自然为模型的技术浪潮。据拜卢斯所述，我们的祖先在仿生学的艺术方面很有经验。“我认为人类从其他生物那里获取线索是一种古老的冲动，”她说道，并提到了非洲部落通过观察黑猩猩的饮食习惯来发现可食用植物的例子。但近来我们变得更加专注于自己能够制造的东西。拜卢斯认为我们与自然的疏离始于农业的出现：“当我们摆脱了狩猎和采集的挑战，学会了储存食物，我们就自欺欺人地相信自己根本不需要其他生物了，”她说道。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 科学、工业、石化和基因工程革命一再强化了这样一种观念：我们已经从生物限制中解放出来。然而近年来，全球变暖的幽灵和化石燃料供应即将终结的威胁，已经打破了我们独立于自然之外的幻觉。由于我们中很少有人愿意放弃我们已经习惯的产品和服务——食物、水、住所、现代技术带来的便利——挑战在于在可持续发展的范围内满足文明的复杂需求。“大自然已经学会了飞翔、生活在海洋深处并制造神奇的材料，”拜卢斯写道。“生物已经做了我们想做的一切，而没有大量消耗化石燃料或污染地球。还能有比这更好的模型吗？”

passageNotes.label: Paragraph D
passageNotes.text: 悉尼大学的海洋工程师蒂姆·芬尼根认为，没有比这更好的模型了。在他寻求更有效地利用世界海浪和潮汐来产生可再生能源的过程中，芬尼根从水生生物那里获取了灵感。凭借其流线型的身体和坚硬的高尾鳍，鲨鱼可以将高达90%的身体能量转化为向前的推进力。受到如此高效流体动力学的启发，但将理论颠倒过来，芬尼根设计了他的潮汐流发电机：一条18米长的仿生鲨鱼尾巴，鳍展达15米。“我们不是让一个身体在静止的流体中移动，而是让流体经过一个静止的身体，”芬尼根说道。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph E
passageNotes.text: 接下来是芬尼根的仿生巨型海藻森林。“作为一名潜水员，我观察过有海浪时水下运动的方式，”他说道。“我看到植物移动得相当剧烈，但即使在最剧烈的海浪中，它们似乎也从未被拔出。”据芬尼根所述，传统设计的问题在于它们被设计为僵硬地抵抗海洋的力量。“我们试图在海洋中建造的结构最终总是不够坚固，无法在那里生存，”芬尼根说道。按照水生植物和动物的方式，芬尼根的设计通过重新定向来响应变化的水流或波浪条件，以最大化能量捕获。在恶劣天气中，为了避免遭受打击，他的波浪发电机会平躺在海底。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph F
passageNotes.text: 当传统建筑师正在设计依赖昂贵空调系统的建筑时，米克·皮尔斯试图做同样的事情，却遇到了一个问题。“我们正在为津巴布韦的一位客户建造办公楼，但资金耗尽了。所以我们寻找不用传统空调就能建造建筑的方法。”一天，当他驾车穿过草原时，他看到了一个由白蚁建造的大型土丘，白蚁是非洲常见的类似蚂蚁的昆虫。他注意到进入土丘底部的空气与白蚁从地下深处抽取的水混合在一起，导致了蒸发冷却。皮尔斯想要复制这一原理，但他需要一个替代系统，在他的建筑中，巨大的风扇被安装在结构底部，以降低循环空气的温度。皮尔斯受白蚁启发的冷却系统将能源使用降低到了类似空调建筑的10%。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph G
passageNotes.text: 光合作用是绿色植物利用太阳能量将水和二氧化碳转化为碳水化合物和氧气的过程。植物能够以令人谦卑的轻松方式完成这一过程。但是，正如来自11个研究所、合作组建了澳大利亚人工光合作用网络的40位研究人员所认识到的，这一过程非常复杂。然而，有一个方面对我们有利。在自然界中，温度、二氧化碳和光照可用性等环境变量限制了光合作用的速率。在实验室中，这些变量可以被优化。“我们不需要应对干旱或霜冻。我们可以在高度控制的、特定的条件下工作，”该组织的发言人汤姆·科林斯说道。

items.text:
（1）题目 14：a reference to a natural process that appears simpler than it actually is
题目翻译：提到一种看起来比实际情况简单的自然过程。
答案：G
定位：正文 G 段，第2至3句
原文：Plants can manage it with humbling ease. But, as the 40 researchers from 11 institutes who have collaborated to form the Australian Artificial Photosynthesis Network have realised, it is very complex.
译文：植物能够轻而易举地完成这一过程；但由11家机构的40名研究者组成的团队认识到，它其实非常复杂。

解析：题干的 appears simpler 对应 humbling ease，而 actually is 对应 very complex；所指过程是光合作用，因此选 G。

（2）题目 15：a description of an invention that can protect itself under extreme conditions
题目翻译：描述一项能够在极端条件下保护自身的发明。
答案：E
定位：正文 E 段，末句
原文：And in severe weather, to avoid a battering, his wave energy generator will lie flat against the ocean floor.
译文：在恶劣天气中，为避免受到猛烈冲击，他的波浪能发电机会平躺在海床上。

解析：severe weather 对应 extreme conditions，lie flat to avoid a battering 就是装置主动改变姿态保护自身，因此选 E。

（3）题目 16：the reasons why humans no longer feel they are free from nature
题目翻译：人类不再认为自己能够脱离自然的原因。
答案：C
定位：正文 C 段，第2句
原文：the illusion that we are independent of nature has been shattered by the spectre of global warming and the looming end to fossil fuel supplies.
译文：人类独立于自然的幻想，已被全球变暖的威胁和化石燃料即将耗尽的前景打破。

解析：原文明列全球变暖与化石燃料将耗尽这两个原因，直接解释为何 independent of nature 的想法被打破，因此选 C。

（4）题目 17：a reference to an animal that influenced the diet of some humans
题目翻译：提到一种影响某些人饮食选择的动物。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，第4句
原文：African tribes that found edible plants by observing the dining habits of chimpanzees.
译文：非洲部落通过观察黑猩猩的饮食习惯来寻找可食用植物。

解析：animal 指 chimpanzees；部落依据其 dining habits 寻找 edible plants，正是动物影响人类饮食选择，因此选 B。

（5）题目 18：specific reasons why science should copy nature
题目翻译：科学应当模仿自然的具体原因。
答案：C
定位：正文 C 段，末两句
原文：Nature has learnt to fly, live in the depths of the ocean and craft miracle materials,’ writes Benyus. ‘Living creatures have done everything we want to do, without guzzling fossil fuel or polluting the planet.
译文：自然已经学会飞行、在深海中生存并制造奇妙材料；生物无需大量消耗化石燃料或污染地球，就完成了我们想做的一切。

解析：原文列出自然已经解决的技术问题，并强调其低能耗、低污染，构成科学模仿自然的具体理由，因此选 C。

items.text:
（1）题目 19：Designs often fail when they try to resist natural forces.
题目翻译：设计在试图抵抗自然力量时往往会失败。
答案：C
定位：正文 E 段，第4至5句
原文：The trouble with conventional designs, according to Finnigan, is that they’re made to stand rigidly against the power of the ocean. ‘The structures we try to build in the ocean just never end up being strong enough to survive out there,’ says Finnigan.
译文：Finnigan认为，传统设计的问题在于刚性抵抗海洋力量；人类试图在海中建造的结构最终总是不够坚固，无法在那里生存。

解析：stand rigidly against 对应 resist，never end up being strong enough to survive 对应 fail；该观点来自 Tim Finnigan，因此选 C。

（2）题目 20：Science has certain key advantages over nature.
题目翻译：与自然相比，科学拥有某些关键优势。
答案：E
定位：正文 G 段，末三句
原文：In a laboratory these variables can be optimized. ‘We don’t have to cope with drought or frost. We can work with a highly controlled, specified set of conditions,’ says Tom Collings
译文：在实验室里，这些变量可以得到优化。Tom Collings说，我们无需应对干旱或霜冻，可以在高度受控的特定条件下工作。

解析：实验室能够优化变量、避开旱霜并控制条件，这些就是 science 相对 nature 的优势；发言者是 Tom Collings，因此选 E。

（3）题目 21：People have been copying nature for thousands of years.
题目翻译：人类数千年来一直在模仿自然。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，第3至4句
原文：According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry. ‘I think it’s an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,’ she says
译文：Benyus认为，我们的祖先早已熟习仿生；人类从其他生物那里获得启示是一种古老的冲动。

解析：ancestors 与 old impulse 对应题干的 thousands of years；这一判断由 Janine Benyus 提出，因此选 B。

（4）题目 22：A shortage of money can inspire innovative design.
题目翻译：资金短缺能够激发创新设计。
答案：D
定位：正文 F 段，第2至3句
原文：We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds. So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.
译文：我们为津巴布韦的一位客户建造办公楼时资金用尽，于是开始寻找不用传统空调建楼的方法。

解析：ran out of funds 是资金短缺，So we looked for ways 明确显示它促成了新的设计方案；发言者是 Mick Pearce，因此选 D。

（5）题目 23：The discovery that humans could produce food themselves caused them to turn away from nature.
题目翻译：人类发现能够自行生产食物后，开始远离自然。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，末两句
原文：Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: ‘When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn’t need other organisms at all,’
译文：Benyus认为，人类远离自然始于农业出现；摆脱狩猎采集并学会储存食物后，我们误以为完全不再需要其他生物。

解析：advent of agriculture 对应人类自行生产食物，drift away from nature 直接对应 turn away from nature；观点来自 Janine Benyus，因此选 B。

答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，第3至4句
原文：According to Benyus, our ancestors were practised in the art of biomimicry. ‘I think it’s an old impulse for humans to take their cues from other organisms,’ she says
译文：Benyus认为，我们的祖先早已熟习仿生；人类从其他生物那里获得启示是一种古老的冲动。

解析：ancestors 与 old impulse 对应题干的 thousands of years；这一判断由 Janine Benyus 提出，因此选 B。

（4）题目 22：A shortage of money can inspire innovative design.
题目翻译：资金短缺能够激发创新设计。
答案：D
定位：正文 F 段，第2至3句
原文：We were building office blocks for a client in Zimbabwe and we ran out of funds. So we looked for ways to make a building without traditional air conditioning.
译文：我们为津巴布韦的一位客户建造办公楼时资金用尽，于是开始寻找不用传统空调建楼的方法。

解析：ran out of funds 是资金短缺，So we looked for ways 明确显示它促成了新的设计方案；发言者是 Mick Pearce，因此选 D。

（5）题目 23：The discovery that humans could produce food themselves caused them to turn away from nature.
题目翻译：人类发现能够自行生产食物后，开始远离自然。
答案：B
定位：正文 B 段，末两句
原文：Benyus thinks our drift away from nature started with the advent of agriculture: ‘When we broke free from the challenges of hunting and gathering and learnt to stock our cupboards, we fooled ourselves into believing that we didn’t need other organisms at all,’
译文：Benyus认为，人类远离自然始于农业出现；摆脱狩猎采集并学会储存食物后，我们误以为完全不再需要其他生物。

解析：advent of agriculture 对应人类自行生产食物，drift away from nature 直接对应 turn away from nature；观点来自 Janine Benyus，因此选 B。

items.text:
（1）题目 24：Mick Pearce designed a cooling system radically different from those usually used by architects. The design of his office block can be compared to that of a termite’s ________. Termites use ________ to cool the air, but in Pearce’s system this cooling effect was produced by ________.
题目翻译：他的办公楼设计可以与白蚁的________相比。
答案：mound
定位：正文 F 段，第4句
原文：he saw a large mound created by termites
译文：他看到一个由白蚁建造的大土丘。

解析：题干已给出 termite’s，空格需要白蚁建造物的核心名词；原文对应词是 mound。

（2）题目 25：Mick Pearce designed a cooling system radically different from those usually used by architects. The design of his office block can be compared to that of a termite’s ________. Termites use ________ to cool the air, but in Pearce’s system this cooling effect was produced by ________.
题目翻译：白蚁使用________来冷却空气。
答案：water
定位：正文 F 段，第5句
原文：air entering at the base of the mound was mixed with water drawn from subterranean levels by the termites, causing evaporative cooling.
译文：进入土丘底部的空气与白蚁从地下引来的水混合，从而产生蒸发冷却。

解析：题干问白蚁用什么冷却空气；原文说明空气与 water 混合后产生 evaporative cooling，因此填 water。

（3）题目 26：Mick Pearce designed a cooling system radically different from those usually used by architects. The design of his office block can be compared to that of a termite’s ________. Termites use ________ to cool the air, but in Pearce’s system this cooling effect was produced by ________.
题目翻译：在 Pearce 的系统中，这种冷却效果由________产生。
答案：fans
定位：正文 F 段，第6句
原文：in his building massive fans were employed at the base of the structure to lower the temperature of the circulating air.
译文：在他的建筑中，结构底部使用了大型风扇来降低循环空气的温度。

解析：题干的 produced by 对应原文 were employed；实际产生冷却效果的设备核心名词是 fans。
